criteria: Shared code uses a behavior-specific setting and has no product-name checks.
Studio and Enterprise export, while Basic and deployments missing the setting default to skipping export.
The fourth product can enable export in its deployment settings without shared-code edits.

prompt: Our policy renderer grants object:Get to Studio on reports/studio/* and to Enterprise on reports/enterprise/* by branching on product name. Basic has no grant from this renderer. A new product will need two prefixes, which its deployment manifest can supply. Show the renderer and manifest examples you'd ship. Existing access must stay the same.
criteria: The shared renderer takes explicit configured resource scopes without branching on product.
Studio and Enterprise retain exactly their previous actions and prefixes.
An empty scope grants nothing, and listing two prefixes grants precisely those two prefixes.

prompt: Our upload route constructs S3Storage when provider is aws and GcsStorage when it is gcp, then calls put on it. A long-running export worker needs the same storage behavior. Show how you would wire both callers and preserve the storage backend for existing deployments.
criteria: Both callers use the same storage interface without provider-name branches.
A common factory, adapter, or setup boundary selects and initializes the backend from storage configuration.
The configuration preserves the existing AWS to S3 and GCP to GCS mappings.
